intro: Step inside, and look up. You are in Hagia Sophia, in İstanbul province, a monastery and church of AD 537: the domed basilica Justinian raised in five years, and for a thousand years the largest enclosed space in the world.
history: Its story begins in fire. In 532 the Nika riots burned the earlier church, and Justinian replaced it with the present building in just five years and ten months. His architects, Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus, were specialists in geometry and mechanics, and the pendentives that carry the dome were applied here at this scale for the first time. After 1453 it became a mosque; in 1935, a museum; and in 2020, a mosque once again.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the main dome, the mosaics, the Sultan's loge, the marble doors and, if you look closely, the Viking inscription.
facts: Did you know? On a marble parapet in the north gallery, a runic inscription reads 'Halfdan carved this'. It was probably scratched by one of the emperor's Varangian guards. The dome stands 55 metres high and 31 metres across, and for a thousand years it covered the largest enclosed space in the world. The ring of forty windows at its base hides its weight and makes it seem to float; Procopius wrote that it looked as if it hung from heaven on a golden chain.
outro: This brings our journey through Hagia Sophia to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
